correctness.rationale: The proof fixes all quantifiers and uses only one non-elementary input: the recent critical-size selection theorem with arbitrary polynomial failure. A blockwise construction is a uniform random permutation by an exact factorial calculation. For prefixes \(m\le N/2\), every exposed residual has size at least \(N/2\), the number of intersected critical blocks is at most \(1+2^{2/p}mN^{-2/p}\), and Minkowski plus Cauchy--Schwarz gives the asserted upper scale. A union bound with a larger failure exponent controls all those blocks simultaneously. For \(m>N/2\), \(L^2\)-\(L^\infty\) interpolation gives the deterministic tail bound \(r^{(1-2/p)/2}\). The Fourier lower bound is uniform over all subsets because every frequency \(1,\ldots,N\) has phase in the same sector on \(|x|\le(12N)^{-1}\).

value.rationale: The quantity \(K_p(S;\Phi)\) is the central finite Lambda(p) constant, and cardinality is the main parameter in Bourgain's theorem. Determining its sharp dependence across every \(m\), rather than only at the critical point, is a natural structural question. The result identifies \(m\asymp N^{2/p}\) as the exact transition from bounded constants to growth, and strengthens existence to a single nested random family that is simultaneously order-optimal at all scales. The Fourier construction shows that this is not merely an artifact of the proof or a one-sided estimate.
